analysis.title: SpaceX: Super Intelligence Singularity; Reiterate Overweight & Raising PT to $500
key_insights: JPM reiterates Overweight on SpaceX (SPCX) and raises the Dec-27 price target from $240 to $500, based on 20x 2028E GAAP EPS of $24.41. Stock closed at $147.79 on 10/20.
3Q26 revenue was $14,575M, +161% y/y and +87% q/q, 6% above JPMe ($13,733M) and 13% above consensus ($12,875M). All three segments beat on revenue.

Super Intelligence (SI, formerly AI) is now the primary driver. SPCX expects to end 2026 with 2-3 GW of compute and to add about 10 GW in 2027, reaching about 13 GW total, above the previously expected 5-10 GW range.
Management says power, cooling and infrastructure constraints are bigger than chip constraints. It is targeting 20 GW of power by end of 2027 and is looking at solar and wind as well as gas.
JPM believes the 10 GW of 2027 incremental compute is almost all Nvidia Vera Rubin. SemiAnalysis puts Vera Rubin monetization about 40% above the strongest GB300s.
Monetization is $30B-$50B per GW today. Management sees $500B-$1T of ARR at end of 2027. JPM models 2027 revenue of $254B, implying about $400B of ending ARR, and 10 GW of compute at end of 2027.
4Q26 capex is guided to $35-40B versus JPM's prior $19B. JPM's 2027 capex estimate rises from about $200B to about $300B.

Management said it is not considering raising equity and has several debt capital pools available. It claims a build cost in the mid-$30B per GW range versus $50B+ for others, and a possible 6-month compute payback next year.
JPM raises 2026E adj. EPS from $0.93 to $1.49 and 2027E from $3.45 to $9.88 (+186%). 2027 and 2028 estimates more than double. JPM acknowledges a lot has to go right to hit them.
SI segment 3Q26 revenue was $7,560M (+830% y/y), 8% above JPMe. SI operating income of $431M (6% margin) missed JPMe of $754M (11% margin). Connectivity operating income of $2,367M beat JPMe by 27%.

Current short-term neocloud contract pricing is slightly above the high end of the $30-50/W range. SPCX targets roughly a 50/50 internal/external split of capacity, which could shift to 60/40 either way. Management said it could rent out its compute several times over.

Starlink added 1.6M consumer subscribers in 3Q26 to reach 13.6M. Consumer ARPU rose 5% q/q to $69 per month. JPM models 4Q net adds of 2.2M and ARPU of $66, and 2027 net adds of 11.5M with ARPU falling 17.4% to $55.42.

Starlink Mobile US launch is still expected in early 2028. Satellite deployment is now the gating item after the agreement to acquire Grain's 800 MHz spectrum. JPM still thinks SPCX will need terrestrial macro towers to compete with the Big-3 carriers.

SPCX will attempt to catch both the Super Heavy booster and the Ship on Starship Flight 15, likely in November. A Ship catch would be a first. Starship flights are expected weekly in 1H27 and semi-weekly in 2H27.

On a possible SPCX-TSLA merger, Musk said both companies formed special committees and there are significant merits, but it would need shareholder approval and there are no guarantees. JPM sees regulatory considerations as a possible factor.
3Q26 free cash flow was -$9,962M versus JPMe of -$3,442M. JPM forecasts $300B+ of negative FCF and debt proceeds over 2026-2030, with positive FCF not modeled until 2031.

market_movers.rationale: PT raised from $240 to $500 on 20x 2028E GAAP EPS of $24.41 after sharply higher compute build and SI monetization estimates. JPM applies an in-line multiple to Mag7 and PLTR peers because of greater execution risk.

earnings_insights: SpaceX 3Q26 reported revenue $14,575M (+161% y/y) vs JPMe $13,733M and consensus $12,875M.
3Q26 reported GAAP EPS $0.35 vs JPMe $0.14 and consensus $0.13.
3Q26 reported GAAP operating income $2,791M vs JPMe $2,394M and consensus $1,208M.
3Q26 reported capex $19,593M vs JPMe $18,584M and consensus $19,604M.
3Q26 reported FCF -$9,962M vs JPMe -$3,442M and consensus -$11,638M.
4Q26 guidance: capex $35-40B vs JPM's prior $19B. JPM estimates 4Q26E revenue $23,974M and adj. EPS $0.75.
JPM estimates (not consensus): FY26E adj. EPS $1.49 (prior $0.93), FY27E $9.88 (prior $3.45), FY28E $27.02. FY27E revenue $254,127M and FY28E $616,492M.
risk_factors: Everything depends on Starship reusability. Delays or regulatory hurdles would affect multiple business lines.
Power and chip supply constraints could delay the compute buildout and weigh on gross margins.
Extremely strong execution is required, and competition from Blue Origin, AMZN and international players is picking up.
Heavy capital intensity and near-term FCF burn: $300B+ of negative FCF and debt proceeds over 2026-2030, with cost overruns possibly raising capital needs despite the $85B+ IPO and $25B debt raised.
Regulatory risk from export controls, ITAR, spectrum allocation and environmental reviews of Starship.
Key-man and governance risk from Musk's concentrated control.
Potential SPCX-TSLA merger requires shareholder approval and carries regulatory uncertainty.
vol_and_positioning: SPCX 90-day volatility is 81. Free float is 37.1%, 3M ADV is 94.58M shares ($13,247.6M), and the 52-week range is $104.83-$225.64.
Elon Musk holds about 82% voting power. SPCX is a controlled company under Nasdaq rules.

tension_points.bull_case: Management is highly confident in 10 GW of incremental compute in 2027, mostly Vera Rubin. It cites mid-$30B/GW build costs, pricing slightly above $50/W, payback under 1 year, and demand it says exceeds capacity several times over.
tension_points.bear_case: JPM says a lot has to go right: building the compute, securing significant capital and a continued strong demand environment. FCF burn of $300B+ over 2026-2030 and power and infrastructure constraints could extend the burn or delay scale.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Delays in the Vera Rubin deployment (440k GPUs targeted by end of 2Q27) or in the 20 GW power buildout, or failure to secure capital, would undermine the 2027 ARR and EPS estimates.

theme_stances.key_argument: Accelerated Vera Rubin compute buildout with elevated monetization supports management's $500B-$1T ARR target and sharply higher JPM estimates.
theme_stances.evidence: Another SpaceX earnings report and another series of significant upward estimate revisions.
